name: Ings weekend (open)
summary: Silent weekend for 8 experienced practitioners on a fellside smallholding. No scheduled sits; the byre, the bell, the fell, and your own timetable. £60.
description:
Ings is a smallholding at the foot of the Howgill Fells with a converted byre sleeping eight. Most weekends from March to October it is open to people who already have a practice and want two days of silence somewhere with a hill.

**Sits**
None scheduled. The byre is open all weekend and people use the cushions and the bell when they choose. Some sit at dawn and dusk because that is what they do at home; some sit three hours at midday; some do not sit in the byre at all and spend both days on the fell. Nobody notices what you do.

**The rest**
No schedule. The fell behind the byre is steep and open and takes most of a day to cross. There is a large wood pile and an axe by the door. The byre has cushions and a bell. The beck runs past the door.

**Silence**
Friday evening to Sunday lunch, including meals, which are left in the byre kitchen for people to eat when they come in.

**Host**
Jen lives in the farmhouse. She does not teach. On Friday evening she shows you where things are and then leaves you to it. If you want to talk, there is a slot on Saturday afternoon; write your name on the board. Most weekends nobody does.

**Level**
Moderately demanding: the fell is real, the wood is heavy, the byre is cold at six. For people who have done a silent retreat before and can spend unstructured hours for two whole days without a teacher or a bell. Not for a first retreat.

**Cost**
£60 per person, including the byre and all food.
practical: Friday 6pm to Sunday 1pm, most weekends March to October. £60 including all food. Eight bunks in one room; bring a sleeping bag. Wood stove, hot water, one shower. Bring boots, waterproofs, work gloves, warm layers. Oxenholme station 14 miles; collection Friday 5pm. No mobile signal.
